output: Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, there is no significant relationship between time preference (as measured by DISSAVED and SAMESAVE) and BMI in Hispanic men. The correlation coefficients between BMI and DISSAVED (r ≈ 0.004) and SAMESAVE (r ≈ 0.106) are very weak, and the regression analysis shows that these variables do not significantly predict BMI (p-values of 0.992 and 0.354, respectively). Therefore, time preference does not appear to have a statistically significant impact on BMI in Hispanic men based on this dataset.
